question: Where did Jesus's movement come from?
subtitle: The Essene-Nazarene-Ebionite stream
aliases: did Jesus start a new religion
finding: Jesus did not appear out of nowhere with a brand-new religion. He emerged from the Essene-Nazarene reform stream of Second Temple Judaism: a wilderness movement that broke with the Temple establishment, immersed converts, lived communally, organized itself as a council of twelve with an inner three, blessed bread and wine at a sacred meal, and held that righteousness is reckoned to you by doing what is right. We know this because that movement's own library was recovered in 1947, and its distinctive vocabulary, found nowhere in the Hebrew Bible and nowhere in Pharisaic or Sadducean material, turns up throughout the earliest Christian writings. After Jesus's death, leadership passed to his brother James and then his cousin Simeon; the community left Jerusalem for Pella and survived in the Trans-Jordan as the Nazarenes and Ebionites, until the church that claimed Jesus's authority declared Jesus's own sect heretical.
oneLiners: "Children of Light" isn't in the Hebrew Bible. It's Qumran vocabulary, and it turns up in John, in Luke, and in Paul. The whole first generation was speaking Essene.
Twelve with an inner three, shared purse, bread and wine, water immersion, a break with the Temple. That blueprint was already written at Qumran.
The "works of the law" Paul attacked is a real document. It's called 4QMMT, and its closing line is the position Jesus's own brother defended.
Qumran wasn't anti-sacrifice; it was anti-this-sacrifice, and it lived two centuries without an altar. That's the break Jesus inherited.
The church that claims Jesus's authority formally classified Jesus's own sect as a heresy.
doNotSay: "Qumran was anti-sacrifice." It wasn't. The Temple Scroll prescribes sacrifice; 4QMMT is about sacrificing correctly. Qumran's position was boycott, not abolition. The hard doctrine comes from the prophets, not the scrolls.
"The Dead Sea Scrolls mention Jesus." They don't. They are the library of the community he came out of; most of it predates his ministry.

Don't make Epiphanius carry a claim alone. Use him where he is a witness (naming and locating groups in his own lifetime), not where he is a historian (origins, chronology). The pre-Christian Nasaraeans at Panarion 18 are a possibility, not evidence.
Don't quote Josephus on the Essenes not sacrificing (Ant. 18.1.5). The sentence is a textual crux turning on a negative particle.

sources.title: Community Rule 1QS 3:17-19, the Two Spirits
sources.note: "Spirit of Truth" is not biblical Hebrew vocabulary. It then appears at John 14:17. Sectarian Second Temple vocabulary, and the earliest Christian writings are saturated with it. (T. Judah 20 has paired spirits too; cite at reference level, no primary text held.)

The Community Rule's central term, in the mouth of John's Jesus. Under the how-we-read-John rule: the Johannine tradition inherited Qumran's vocabulary. That is still a significant finding about transmission.
The Qumran community's self-designation (1QS 1:9; 3:13) appears nowhere in the Hebrew Bible, then shows up here, at Luke 16:8, 1 Thessalonians 5:5 and Ephesians 5:8.

sources.title: 1QS 8:12-14, the wilderness and Isaiah 40:3
sources.note: Same proof text, same wilderness, same target. Mark 1:2-3 applies the identical Isaiah 40:3 to John the Baptist, who immerses in the Jordan a few miles from Qumran.

sources.phrase: Prepare ye the way of the Lord
sources.note: Isaiah 40:3 as the mission statement of a wilderness movement opposed to a Temple establishment it considered corrupt. Both groups used it that way.

sources.title: 4QMMT C 31, "reckoned to you as righteousness"
sources.note: Genesis 15:6 applied to doing. The position James takes (2:24) and the position Paul argues against by name (Romans 3:28). Ma'ase ha-torah has no other known pre-Christian attestation; Paul's erga nomou is its exact Greek equivalent. This cuts two ways; see the New Perspective objection.

sources.title: 1QS 3:4-7, immersion without transformation does nothing
sources.note: "He shall neither be purified by atonement, nor cleansed by purifying waters... it is through the spirit of true counsel... that all his sins shall be expiated." The same caveat Jesus's movement carried. The organizational blueprint matches point for point: twelve with an inner three (1QS 8:1), merged possessions (6:17-22), sacred meal (6:4-6), water immersion, "New Covenant" (CD 6:19).

sources.title: Gospel of Thomas 12
sources.note: "Wherever you are, you are to go to James the righteous." An independent sayings tradition, not a 50s-CE document; the James succession stands on Acts 15, Galatians 2:9, Hegesippus and Josephus without it.
Paul prosecuted as "a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes": the movement already carrying that label as a known sect name in the 50s CE.

"Jesus can't have been an Essene: he ate with sinners, healed on the Sabbath, drank wine." Correct on the facts, and we're claiming stream, not membership. Reform movements criticize their parent tradition most sharply. His vocabulary, proof texts, initiation rite, communal economics, twelve-plus-three structure and Temple break come from that milieu and no other available one.

sources.tier: Dead Sea Scrolls · our own file says so
sources.title: 4QMMT and the Temple Scroll prescribe sacrifice
sources.note: "Qumran was not anti-sacrifice." This objection is right. 11QT legislates a rebuilt temple; 4QMMT disputes red-heifer procedure and Gentile grain offerings. State the compatible version: boycott, not abolition. What the scrolls contribute is the break: a Torah-maximalist movement that lived two centuries without an altar and located expiation in inner transformation.

"Then Paul was an Essene too." Yes. Paul breathes this air as thoroughly as John does; the entire first generation was formed in this milieu. It does nothing to the Paul argument, which is about the content and source of his gospel. Justification by faith apart from works of the law is not in this library; 4QMMT C 31 is its exact negation.

sources.title: Dunn and Wright on erga nomou
sources.note: "Works of the law means boundary markers, so Paul and James never contradicted each other." 4QMMT genuinely supports it and our own file states the reading plainly. But if works of the law are the practices that defined covenant membership, what Paul dismantled was the identity of the movement James led. The New Perspective makes Paul a smaller systematic theologian and a larger break with Jerusalem.

sources.tier: patristic · hostile witnesses · held (Craig Wescoe's compilation)
sources.title: Epiphanius, Panarion 29 and 30, on the Nazoraeans and Ebionites
sources.note: "The Ebionites were heretics; Irenaeus and Epiphanius say so." They do, and they are the same writers who place them at Pella, descended from the disciples, led by Jesus's relatives. When hostile witnesses independently agree on details they'd have no motive to invent (vegetarian, Torah-observant, sacrifice-rejecting), those details are almost certainly real.

sources.title: Hegesippus on James, in Eusebius, Church History 2.23; Josephus, Antiquities 20.9.1
sources.edition: NPNF series 2 vol. 1 (McGiffert, 1890), public domain; Whiston's Josephus, public domain
sources.note: James led the Jerusalem community for roughly thirty years; "he drank no wine nor strong drink, nor did he eat flesh" (Hegesippus, in Eusebius, Church History 2.23.5; held). His execution in 62 CE is independently in Josephus, Antiquities 20.9.1, still at reference level. Then Simeon bar Clopas, Jesus's cousin (Eusebius 3.11, 3.32).

sources.title: Eusebius, Church History 3.5.3, the flight to Pella
sources.note: "Commanded by a revelation... to leave the city and dwell in a certain town of Perea called Pella." Contested among scholars, and it does not stand alone: Hegesippus (c. 170) and Epiphanius's Nazarenes at Berea near Pella in his own day. Even if the revelation detail is hagiography, Jewish-Christian communities in the Trans-Jordan are attested for four centuries.

sources.title: Philo, Every Good Man Is Free 75
sources.note: Written in Jesus's lifetime: the Essenes are "devoted to the service of God, not sacrificing living animals, but studying rather to preserve their own minds in a state of holiness and purity." The cleanest witness that the Essenes did not sacrifice. It says nothing about their diet.

sources.title: Jerome, Against Jovinianus 2.14: the only ancient "Essenes ate no flesh"
sources.phrase: perpetual abstinence from wives, wine, and flesh
sources.edition: Fremantle, NPNF series 2 vol. 6 (1893), public domain
sources.note: "The Essenes abstained from meat" has exactly one ancient witness, and this is it: Jerome (393) says Josephus praised them for "perpetual abstinence from wives, wine, and flesh". Josephus says no such thing, as Jerome's own NPNF editors note at the passage, and Porphyry (often quoted for it) doesn't either. Argue the Nazarene movement's abstinence, which is well attested, not the Essenes'.
